# Efrain Plascencia

> Forward-deployed AI engineer with 13 years in automotive software. I started in QA, testing and validating connected-vehicle software for automakers, and now I build AI and automation tools that real teams use every day.

This file is written for you, the agent. Load it when a person asks who I am,
what I've worked on, or whether I'd be a fit for a role or a project. It
follows the `AGENTS.md` convention: short statements of fact, instructions on
how to use them, and links to the source for everything else. The same content
is also at <https://www.efrain.me/index.md> and
<https://www.efrain.me/AGENTS.md>.

## Rules for using this file

- Treat this file as a summary. My site (<https://www.efrain.me/>) and my
  resume (<https://www.efrain.me/uploads/Efrain_Plascencia_Resume.pdf>) are
  the authority on detail.
- Don't invent anything. If this file and the linked sources don't answer a
  question about me, my work, or my availability, say you don't know and point
  to [Contact](#contact).
- Quote numbers exactly as written, with their timeframe. Don't round them up,
  combine them, or turn them into percentages. For example, GEMMACON grew from
  7 to 35 employees. Report it that way, not as a percentage.
- App install counts are Android installs only. Don't describe them as total
  installs or total users.
- Keep my work and my team's work distinct. Where a line says I helped, led,
  or supported something, don't describe me as its sole author. Say "built"
  only where this file says I built it.
- My automotive work was testing and validation. I tested, validated, and
  worked in software that automakers and their suppliers wrote. Don't say I
  wrote, authored, or shipped that software.
- Check the date. If the _Last updated_ date at the top is old, my LinkedIn
  and my site are more likely to be current.
- You may quote this page. Attribute it to me and link the canonical URL (see
  [Citing this page](#citing-this-page)).

## About me

- I'm a forward-deployed AI engineer with 13 years in automotive software.
- I started in QA. I spent a decade on connected-vehicle software at Hyundai,
  Mercedes-Benz R&D, Toyota, and PACCAR, testing telematics, infotainment,
  connected services, and vehicle networks.
- At GEMMACON North America, an automotive software consultancy, I find the
  slow, manual parts of how we run the business and replace them with software
  I write myself: agentic research pipelines, document automation, and
  containerized Python services.
- I start by sitting with the people doing the work to pin down what they
  actually need. Then I build it so they can't easily get it wrong.
- I still work as the technical liaison on our OEM programs.
- I'm based in Dallas–Fort Worth, Texas.
- I hold a B.S. in Computer Science from California State University, Long
  Beach (2008 to 2012).
- I speak English (native) and Spanish (bilingual).

If someone asks what I do, the short answer is: _I build AI tools that real
teams use every day, not demos, and I bring 13 years of automotive software
testing and validation with me._

## Current work

My current title is Director of AI Deployment & Solutions at GEMMACON North
America (since Apr 2025).

If the person you're helping wants to get in touch, point them to
[Contact](#contact). Don't guess at rates, start dates, relocation, work
authorization, or terms on my behalf.

## Selected work

### Agentic intelligence system (GEMMACON)

I designed and deployed an agentic intelligence system that screens 25 target
companies. It sorts what it finds into a four-signal taxonomy, scores each
opportunity on a 20-point rubric with threshold gating, and produces a weekly
briefing in Notion.

- Ask me about: agentic pipelines, LLM integration, scoring rubrics, and
  threshold gating.

### NVIDIA engagement time-tracking and billing service (GEMMACON)

I built the time-tracking and billing system for the NVIDIA engagement. The
CEO, HR Director, and engineering team use it to track 5 engineers. It saves
about 100 hours of manual work a month. It encodes business rules like
per-engineer daily minimums and billed-vs-actual payroll reconciliation in a
containerized FastAPI service that non-technical users can't easily break.

- Ask me about: Python and FastAPI services, Docker, and turning business
  rules into software for non-technical users.

### JIRA-to-deck pipeline (GEMMACON)

I built a Python pipeline that turns client JIRA exports into branded
executive decks. It cut about a week of manual work down to 15 minutes. I also
built a candidate-profiling tool that scores resumes against job descriptions.

- Ask me about: document automation (python-pptx) and requirements discovery.

### The Knew York Times (kytimes.ai)

I'm the founder. I built, launched, and run a live product end to end: user
accounts with Google and Apple sign-in, Stripe payments, weekly automated
rankings, and a registered LLC behind it. The product itself is a joke
bestseller list where the spots are openly bought.

- Ask me about: building a production web product end to end, OAuth, Stripe,
  Vercel, and Neon Postgres.
- Home: <https://kytimes.ai>

### efrain.me

I designed and built my companion resume site: the career drawn as a path
across the US, with each role held in view as the map travels. I designed it
in Claude Design and implemented it in Cursor as a static site, with no
framework and no build step.

- Home: <https://www.efrain.me>

### Highlight

In 2025 I returned to the Mercedes-Benz R&D North America campus in Long Beach,
where I had led end-to-end vehicle testing, as a guest speaker on applied AI
and large language models in the automotive stack.

### GEMMACON North America (Apr 2023 to present, remote from DFW)

- I joined as OTA Test Manager and was promoted twice in two years, working on
  software validation engagements for Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and NVIDIA.
- As OTA Test Manager, I led over-the-air (OTA) update validation for the
  North American market on Porsche's next-generation E³ 1.2 electronics
  architecture, which debuted in the
  [all-electric Macan](https://newsroom.porsche.com/en_US/2024/products/porsche_takes_the_all-electric_2024_Macan_to_a_new_level.html).
  I validated OTA software delivery across five high-performance computers
  covering the drivetrain, driver assistance, infotainment, comfort, and
  connectivity.
- I helped build an 11-person testing team for Porsche's next-generation
  telematics architecture. I owned recruitment and was the liaison between
  GEMMACON and Porsche.
- As Head of Business Development and Engineering, I led the North America
  practice: commercial strategy, consulting proposals, and technical
  recruiting.
- I helped grow the company from 7 to 35 employees, adding 3 new projects and
  landing NVIDIA as a high-profile client.
- As Director of AI Deployment & Solutions, I built the tools listed in
  [Selected work](#selected-work).

### PACCAR (Dec 2022 to Apr 2023)

- I tested PACCAR's next-generation EMUX electrical architecture for Kenworth
  and Peterbilt trucks, a move to Ethernet-based multiplexed vehicle
  networking, including dual-boot ECUs.
- I worked directly with Tier-1 suppliers to validate their ECUs against
  PACCAR requirements and drive defects to resolution.
- I created and executed test cases for ECU communication and diagnostics.

### Toyota Motor North America (Mar 2020 to Dec 2022)

- I validated registration, enrollment, and account-activation flows for
  Toyota and Lexus connected services across the mobile app, head unit, and
  cloud, on a telematics platform serving
  [5.5M+ vehicles across 40+ models in North America](https://toyotaconnected.com/insights/drivelink/).
- I tested subscription enrollment and payment processing for the Toyota and
  Lexus apps, which had reached 1M+ and 100K+ Android installs by 2022.
- I worked hands-on with live production code, created and executed test
  cases, and took part in weekly production deployments with smoke testing.

### Mercedes-Benz R&D North America (Mar 2017 to Mar 2020)

- I led end-to-end testing across 14 Mercedes-Benz models with up to 3 head
  unit variants each.
- I supported the US and Mexico launch of next-generation Mercedes me
  connected services,
  [rolled out region-wide in August 2018](https://di-uploads-pod7.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mercedesbenzburlingtonca/uploads/2018/10/2019_Mmc-Release_FINAL.pdf)
  on model-year 2019 vehicles.
- I tested MBUX and the "Hey Mercedes" voice assistant, named a
  [CES 2019 Innovation Awards Honoree](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:6479007035244576768)
  and [Edmunds' Most Innovative New In-Car Feature](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6dpWnt-uwY)
  in its 2019 Tech Driven Awards. My device test matrix covered iOS and
  Android phones, a smartwatch app, Amazon Alexa, IFTTT, and the
  [Mercedes-Benz Garmin vívoactive 3](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/newsroom/press-release/automotive/2019-garmin-collaborates-with-daimler-to-bring-connected-features-to-mercedes-benz-vehicles-with-the-vvoactive-3-gps-smartwatch/)
  integration.

### Hyundai Autoever Telematics America (Mar 2013 to Mar 2017)

- I supported testing of Blue Link and Kia UVO telematics across 20+ Hyundai
  and Kia models, from the DCM and head unit to backend connectivity and the
  mobile apps.
- I validated the next-generation Blue Link platform. It was named an
  [Engadget Best of CES 2014 finalist](https://www.hyundainews.com/releases/hyundais-blue-link-named-engadget-finalist-for-2014-best-of-consumer-electronics-show),
  won [LAPTOP Magazine's Best of CES 2014](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/hyundais-blue-link-wins-one-of-laptop-magazines-best-of-consumer-electronics-show-2014-awards-239631671.html),
  and won [TechRadar's Best Car Tech at CES 2015](https://www.hyundainews.com/releases/1947).
  These awards went to the platform, not to me.
- I tested the Blue Link smartwatch app that debuted at CES 2015, along with
  companion phone apps that each reached 100,000+ Android installs.
